A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ARNCG research and contain readable text, algorithms, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Material can be reliably matched across the extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix F report original CUTEst comparisons, parameter ablations and local-convergence experiments.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendices G–H retain the CUTEst experiments and add original physics-informed neural network training results.

M1.justification: The central regularizers, fallback logic, capped CG and linesearch procedures remain unchanged; LipEstimation separates previously inline update rules. Appendix H.1 adds randomized Nyström preconditioning to CG for the PINN implementation, a limited procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: v3 retains the 124 CUTEst problems and adds PINN training for convection, reaction and wave PDEs. This substantially extends evaluation from conventional optimization benchmarks to neural approximation of physical equations.

E2.justification: v3 adds adaptive cubic regularization method ARCqK to the CUTEst comparisons and NNCG with regularization coefficients 0.1 and 0.01 to the new PINN comparisons. CAT and AN2CER remain. Adam and L-BFGS serve as shared preliminary training stages.

E3.justification: The added PINN experiments introduce an 81,201-parameter network, 10,000 residual training points, a 101×257 evaluation mesh, Adam/L-BFGS warm starts and final-stage time budgets of 7.5, 2 and 18 hours. Training loss and test relative error are new evaluation metrics. The existing CUTEst tolerance, iteration limit and time limit remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The fallback, regularization-exponent and linesearch sweeps, together with the HIMMELBG and ROSENBR local-convergence cases, are retained from Appendix F as Appendix G. Their tested questions and reported outcomes remain unchanged; the added PINN material supplies optimizer comparisons rather than a new targeted ablation or robustness study.

E5.justification: v1 reports benchmark aggregates without repeated-seed uncertainty. v3 introduces eight random-seed runs per PINN experiment, mean and individual trajectories, and mean-plus-standard-deviation results in Table 7. Checklist item 7 identifies the uncertainty as standard deviation and explicitly describes CUTEst experiments as deterministic.

E6.justification: Existing CUTEst table entries are unchanged, while Tables 3–6 add ARCqK results, including 16.16 s shifted geometric mean runtime and 87.10% success. Tables 2 and 7 and Figures 3 and 7 add substantial PINN results. For example, Table 7 reports reaction mean training loss of 2.04×10^-9 for ARNCGg versus 5.20×10^-8 for NNCG0.01.

T1.justification: The principal assumptions, complexity guarantees and appendix proofs are retained or relocated. Section 3 adds an argument about a theta-independent neighborhood with order-3/2 convergence and a K1+K2 bound on additional iterations before quadratic convergence. This is a limited theoretical refinement.

C1.justification: The central claims of adaptive regularization, optimal global complexity and quadratic local convergence remain. The abstract and introduction extend the practical contribution to competitive training of medium-scale PINNs, without replacing the original theoretical contribution.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the PINN advantages through globalization and adaptive regularization. Appendix A.2 newly identifies multiple CG iterations as a computational limitation and notes that nonsmooth activations such as ReLU may violate the Hessian assumption. The earlier CUTEst tradeoffs and failure-mode discussion remain.

D1.justification: Appendix H adds substantial implementation information: Python version, P100 GPUs, network architecture, double precision, tanh activation, Xavier initialization, sampling mesh, preconditioning and optimizer schedules. Appendix G adds the ARCqK implementation source. The checklist promises a code release, but the PDFs do not establish that release occurred.

R1.justification: The earlier related-work discussion is substantially expanded in Appendix A.1, distinguishing regularization, linesearch, adaptivity and proof techniques from Royer, He, Gratton and trust-region methods. v3 also adds positioning against adaptive cubic regularization and PINN optimization literature, including Dussault, Rathore and Nyström-preconditioning work.

P1.justification: The abstract and introductory framing are rewritten, Section 2.1 substantially expands the method's intuition, and Section 3 reorganizes the technical narrative. Related work and the summarized descent lemma move into appendices. These changes substantially restructure existing exposition beyond simply adding experiments.

P2.justification: v3 adds PINN Figures 3 and 7 and Tables 2 and 7, expands CUTEst displays with ARCqK, and revises the theoretical comparison table. Conference formatting substantially resizes and repositions displays, while algorithm formatting adds line numbers and a separate LipEstimation block.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the practical evidence beyond v1's CUTEst evaluation through three PINN tasks, a specialist comparator, matched time budgets and eight-seed uncertainty reporting. ARCqK also makes the existing benchmark comparison more informative. Expanded method explanations and explicit applicability limits improve assessment of the largely unchanged theoretical contribution. The PINN evidence remains limited to three PDE settings, but the combined gains in empirical support and clarity are substantial.
